academic_translation: it would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
translation: It would be clinging to a living being, clinging to a life, and clinging to a person.

academic_translation: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those abiding without affliction,
translation: Blessed One, the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha has said I am the best of those staying without troubling feeling.

academic_translation: Blessed One, although I am an arhat free from desire, Blessed One, I do not think, 'I am an arhat.'
translation: Blessed One, even though I am a worthy one free from wanting, Blessed One, I do not think, 'I am a worthy one.'

academic_translation: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained arhatship,' the Tathāgata, concerning me, would not declare: 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction,' —
translation: Blessed One, if I thought, 'I have gained the state of a worthy one,' the Thus-Gone One would not say about me: 'The son of a good family Subhuti is the best of those staying without troubling feeling.'

academic_translation: Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, the Tathāgata does not declare me 'abiding without affliction'.
translation: Because I do not stay in anything at all, the Thus-Gone One does not say I am 'staying without troubling feeling'.

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata obtained from the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara?"
translation: Do you think the Thus-Gone One got any thing at all from the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha Dipankara?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so.

academic_translation: There is absolutely no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata obtained from the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara."
translation: There is no thing at all that the Thus-Gone One got from the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha Dipankara."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I will accomplish the arrays of Buddha-fields,' he would be speaking untruthfully.
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, if any awakening hero says, 'I will complete the arrangement of Buddha-lands,' they would not be telling the truth.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of Buddha-fields, arrays of Buddha-fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught those arrays as non-arrays.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, the Thus-Gone One taught that what are called "arrangements of Buddha-lands, arrangements of Buddha-lands" are not arrangements.

academic_translation: Therefore, they are called "arrays of Buddha-fields".
translation: Therefore, they are called "arrangements of Buddha-lands."

academic_translation: Subhūti, therefore, a bodhisattva great being should generate the mind in this way, without abiding:
translation: Therefore, Subhuti, a great awakening hero should set the mind like this, without sticking anywhere:

academic_translation: They should generate the mind without abiding in anything whatsoever.
translation: They should set the mind without sticking to anything at all.

academic_translation: They should generate the mind without abiding in form.
translation: They should set the mind without sticking to shapes.

academic_translation: One should generate the mind without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and phenomena.
translation: They should set the mind without sticking to sounds, smells, tastes, things that are touched, or things.

academic_translation: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, if a person were to have a body like this, that is, if it were to become as large as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, Subhūti, what do you think? Would you think that body is large?

locked_terms.use: Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains

translation: "Subhuti, it is like this. Imagine if a person had a body as big as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains. Subhuti, what do you think? Would you think that body is big?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that body would be large.
translation: Subhuti answered, "Blessed One, that body would be big."

academic_translation: Sugata, that body would be large.
translation: "Well-Gone One, that body would be big."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because the Tathāgata has taught that it is no entity.
translation: "Why is that? Because the Thus-Gone One has taught that it is not a real object."

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called a large body.
translation: "That is why it is called a big body."

academic_translation: Because it is no entity, therefore it is called a body.
translation: "Because it is not a real object, that is why it is called a body."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: If there were exactly as many Gaṅgā rivers as there are grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river, do you think that the grains of sand in them would be many?
translation: If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, would there be many grains of sand in all of them?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, if those Gaṅgā rivers themselves would be many, what need is there to speak of their grains of sand?
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, if the Ganges Rivers themselves were that many, we would not even need to speak of their sand!"

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, you should take an interest.
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, you should listen closely.

academic_translation: You should understand.
translation: You should understand.

academic_translation: If some man or woman were to completely fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in those Gaṅgā rivers with the seven precious substances,
translation: If a man or woman completely filled as many world realms as there are grains of sand in those Ganges Rivers with the seven precious things,"

academic_translation: and were to give them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that man or woman generate much merit on that basis?
translation: and gave them as a gift to the Thus-Gone Ones, the worthy ones, and the complete Buddhas. Subhuti, what do you think? Would that man or woman create a lot of stored-up goodness from that?

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, Blessed One, it would be much.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, it would be a lot."

academic_translation: Sugata, it would be much.
translation: "Well-Gone One, it would be a lot."

academic_translation: That man or woman would generate much merit on that basis.
translation: "That man or woman would create a lot of stored-up goodness from that."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, Subhūti, if someone were to completely fill that many world systems with the seven precious substances,
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, if someone completely filled that many world realms with the seven precious things,

academic_translation: compared to giving them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, if someone were to take up even merely a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse, perfectly and thoroughly explain it to others, and perfectly and thoroughly teach it, that very person would generate much more merit on that basis, countless and immeasurable.
translation: and gave them as a gift to the Thus-Gone Ones, the worthy ones, and the complete Buddhas. Now, what if someone else learned even just a four-line verse from this lesson on the teaching? If they fully explained and taught it to others, they would create much more stored-up goodness from that. It would be countless and impossible to measure."

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and demigods, it goes without saying that whoever takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will become endowed with supreme wonder;

locked_terms.use: world with its gods, people, and jealous gods

translation: Also, Subhuti, think of a place where someone recites or teaches even a four-line verse from this lesson on the teaching. That place becomes a shrine for the world with its gods, people, and jealous gods. So, it goes without saying that any human who takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, masters, and carefully thinks about this lesson on the teaching will be filled with the greatest wonder!

academic_translation: in that place resides the Teacher, or someone like a guru.
translation: In that place lives the Teacher, or someone like a master.

academic_translation: When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
translation: When this was said, honored Subhuti said this to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: “Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma discourse?
translation: "Blessed One, what is the name of this lesson on the teaching?

academic_translation: How should I hold it?”
translation: How should I hold it?"

academic_translation: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: When this was said, the Blessed One said this to honored Subhuti:
